recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No core source follow-up is needed for FHIR-5835; future changes to shared request-status definitions should be handled as a separate workflow/terminology decision.
issue_request: FHIR-5835 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification DSTU1 OO change request asking to add a draft or under-preparation status to NutritionOrderStatus, defined as a request in preliminary form before being sent.
initial_application: Git 0e56277ba813b7ae74e753c67355edbc1dc1b07e explicitly preapplied #5625 and #5835 to the NutritionOrderStatus value set, adding the draft row with the requested original definition. The later 33b409a4b6d544598262f2f074ebb4b6dc466157 source rework preserved the status through the modern NutritionOrder StructureDefinition and shared request-status CodeSystem/ValueSet.
additional_context: In current fhir.ini, NutritionOrder is active while NutritionRequest is only a removed historical name. NutritionOrder.status still carries bindingName NutritionOrderStatus, required-binds to ValueSet/request-status, and lists draft in the status short code list. The shared RequestStatus draft definition is generalized to "created but not yet complete or ready for action," which preserves the issue's preliminary/pre-sent meaning. FHIR-5625 confirms the same value-set application path, while already-published audits for FHIR-3720 and FHIR-10297 support the current RequestStatus/request-pattern representation.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source already satisfies FHIR-5835, and changing the shared RequestStatus wording or reintroducing a resource-specific NutritionOrderStatus code system would be broader than this applied DSTU1 issue.

related_jiras.note: The OO block vote for NutritionOrderStatus definitions explicitly included applying FHIR-5835; it was context only and was not decided here.
A later/current combined-branch audit corrected NutritionOrder.status prose to align with requester-controlled request lifecycle state.
An existing combined-branch audit confirms current NutritionOrder/request status alignment through the shared request-status binding.
